captions.text: In 2038, some computers will think it's !1901.!
captions.say: In twenty thirty-eight, some computers will think it's nineteen-oh-one.

captions.text: They count time in seconds since January 1st, 1970.
captions.say: They count time in seconds since January first, nineteen seventy.

captions.text: And many store that count in a signed *32-bit* number.
captions.say: And many store that count in a signed thirty-two-bit number.
Its limit: about two point one billion seconds.
That runs out on January nineteenth, twenty thirty-eight.

captions.text: One second later, the top bit !flips.!
And the clock jumps back to !1901.!
captions.say: And the clock jumps back to nineteen-oh-one.

captions.text: Most modern systems moved to *64-bit* time, good for 292 billion years.
captions.say: Most modern systems moved to sixty-four-bit time, good for two hundred ninety-two billion years.

captions.text: But old devices and forgotten code are still counting toward !2038.!
captions.say: But old devices and forgotten code are still counting toward twenty thirty-eight.
